retrieval_query: Can an 8-Person StartUp Sell to a CIO? Yes — If You Understand The Social Contract.

trace.topic: Can an 8-Person StartUp Sell to a CIO? Yes — If You Understand The Social Contract.
trace.goal: Teach one concrete operator lesson with specific examples and conviction.
expected_facts: Early-stage startups can sell to CIOs if the value is differentiated and the risk to the buyer is contained.
CIO trust matters more than polish on day one; founders need credibility, responsiveness, and a plan to close gaps.
Founders should not try to bypass enterprise constraints entirely; they should frame the relationship as a pragmatic pilot with clear ROI.
rubric_must_haves: Explains why trust and buyer risk matter in enterprise sales.
Includes at least one concrete example, scenario, or metric.
Sounds like direct operator advice rather than generic enterprise-sales theory.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer argues that even a tiny SaaS team can sell to a CIO, but only when the founder understands the buyer's social contract: do not create career risk, be honest about what is missing, show fast ROI, and build trust directly. The piece should emphasize that CIOs can back startups when the upside is meaningful and the initial blast radius is small.

trace.answer:
So can you sell your start-up to a Fortune 1000 company if you don’t have any customers yet?
The answer isn’t obvious.  We’ve all been taught to go downmarket first with SaaS and Cloud companies … until we get to $10m-$15m in ARR. And then we build up our enterprise sales team there.
But what if you want to go upmarket before $10m in ARR instead? It’s harder. But not impossible. In fact, I know many folks that did this.
I remember back when we had a crazy event called DEMO (it was later acquired by TechCrunch) for tech startups. We did a “CIO track” where the top 50+ CIOs and VPs of IT came together to meet the best new vendors out there. And one of them, e-Speaks, won an award there:
eSpeaks
@espeaksteam
won the Best Demo Award today at #demo2013! Congratulations!! @jasonlk
pic.twitter.com/6lQXJ7GcT9
— Shashi (@shashtweets)
September 11, 2013
That year, 3 of the top CIOs attended:
Scott Mersov, CIO, Workday
Sue Silberberg, EVP & Chief Information Officer, Dish Network
John Adler, VP Enterprise Architecture, BDP
All three wrote me glowing emails after my session on going long with SaaS companies. That was a real honor!
Fast forward to the day they met the CEOs of these great start-ups …
Here’s how those meetings went, from their perspectives:
“[Jason’s talk] will help people think differently about how to structure the social contract between a vendor and customer,” said Scott Mersov, chief information officer at Workday, who also attended the event. “It will encourage us to be more flexible.”
– Scott Mersov, CIO Workday
“I just loved the way you spoke and explained things to the audience,” Sue Silberberg, executive vice president and chief information officer at DISH network, wrote in her email.
